subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finbot.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finbot.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for a constructive conversation earlier — appreciate the time. Below is a short recap to make sure we captured your priorities correctly and to propose next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

What we heard (primary pains)
- Inference unit economics are the biggest blocker: current cost per inference is driving ROI concerns for expanding features.
- High throughput (3M calls/month projected) with large variance in request size (avg ~120 tokens, spikes to 800+ tokens) is causing batch inefficiencies.
- Current stack is self-hosted on AWS with a mix of Triton + homegrown orchestration; you’ve hit limits on autoscaling and effective batching.
- Openness to quantization for cost savings but need strict quality/regression thresholds.

Success criteria
- ~2x reduction in cost-per-call (or equivalent unit-economics improvement) at parity of quality.
- P99 latency under 200ms for the majority of low-latency routes; acceptable tail behavior for longer generations.
- Smooth pilot (one month) for 1-2 high-volume endpoints, with clear rollback/fallback.

Initial ideas we discussed (how Redwood could help)
- Intelligent batching + prefix/KV caching for recurring flows to lower per-token cost.
- Quantization profiles and model selection guidance to trade off cost vs. quality.
- Dedicated routing policies for latency-sensitive vs. cost-sensitive traffic.
- Pilot with a single high-volume endpoint to validate savings and monitor quality regressions via evals.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical intake: share sample traffic profile + a small set of prompt examples and logs (see items requested below).
2) Redwood to prepare a tailored pilot plan and rough cost delta estimate (2-3 business days after intake).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Ben (solutions) to walk through inference topology and batching expectations.

Items we requested from you (can share in reply or via Drive):
- Example prompt set (5-10 samples) and expected outputs for quality checks.
- Recent infra summary: instance types, average tokens/request, concurrency.
- Any existing throughput/cost dashboards or spreadsheets.

Attachments: initial-ma-demo-plan.pdf (high-level pilot outline)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options for the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference — developer-first platform for low-latency, cost-efficient LLM inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finbot.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 18:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: ~3M inference calls/month across a mix of synchronous and async endpoints.
- Avg tokens/request: ~120; median lower, but spikey because we have some long-form generation.
- Current infra: mostly AWS (self-hosted), Triton-based serving plus a custom queueing layer. We’ve started experimenting with smaller instance types but haven’t seen linear cost savings because of batching inefficiencies.
- Quantization: open to it, but legal & product want to validate output quality on a per-model basis before roll.

We’ll share: an anonymized sample of prompts + a small dataset (5-10 prompts) and an infra snippet. Priya will own sending the items early next week.

Also — please include a rough estimate in the pilot plan for potential cost delta (ballpark) so execs have something to react to.

Appreciate it,
Samir
VP Product | FinBot
samir@finbot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finbot.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finbot.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Samir.

Ben — looping you in here to coordinate the technical deep-dive. Proposed availability: Wed 12/09 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 12/10 13:00-14:00 PT. Let us know what works and we’ll lock a calendar invite.

We’ll aim to produce a short cost-delta estimate with two scenarios: (A) conservative (software + caching + modest quant), (B) aggressive (quantization + model distill/selection). Expect the deck + MLP by EOD Tue 12/08 after we receive the sample prompts.

Items Priya will share: anonymized prompt set + a small traffic extract. If you can also provide a simple CSV of monthly volume by endpoint, that will speed up our modeling.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP scope + timeline)

Thanks all — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Samir / Priya — Ben here, Solutions Engineer. Quick note on what I’ll want for the technical session:

- Sample traffic (CSV): timestamp, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, success/failure flag.
- One or two representative prompts + expected output for fidelity checks.
- Any existing batching config or Triton pipeline YAMLs you can share.

If you can drop those items into the Drive folder in Marissa’s link (or reply to this thread), I’ll pre-run a quick batching/caching model to illustrate expected savings.

Looking forward to the call — I’ll prepare a live demo of how our KV prefix caching and continuous batching affects unit cost.
